findings.reason: without an edge or a queued build naming §30 the plan claims to be heading for a state no dispatch reaches, the same unreachable-section defect already repaired for §29 and §22.
findings.text: §30 is declared `implementable` while no dependency edge and no followup names it: `plan-section-depends-on` carries s26 and s27 only, and the sole open followup `f-hpdw-013` names §22, §24, §28, §29, §26 and §27 — so no dispatch will ever name §30 and its deliverable is unreachable

findings.reason: the node's only measure cannot be constructed as written, so the worker has to invent the tolerance the section exists to fix.
findings.text: the failing-first arm requires a lock held "longer than sqlite's default and less than the index refresh's busy timeout", but `INDEX_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 0.2` (reckon/run_store.py:152) is twenty-five times shorter than sqlite's 5 s default, so no lock duration satisfies the clause; the refusal arm then says "held past that bound" without naming which bound, leaving the two arms unseparable

findings.reason: a worker following the stated cause adds a per-attempt busy timeout that already exists and never touches the total retry bound, so a lock held past 3 s still refuses and the observed failure reproduces after the section closes.
findings.text: the named cause does not match the writer behind the cited error: a promoted run is written through `run_store.append`, which delegates to `_retrying` and opens `RunStore(busy_timeout=INDEX_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` (0.2 s per attempt) inside a `INDEX_RETRY_SECONDS = 3.0` wall-clock backoff, so the write gives up on that 3 s bound and not on sqlite's 5 s default; the claim that "only the index refresh passes `INDEX_BUSY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`" is false because `append` and `import_ledger` pass it through the same helper, and `tests/test_a_locked_ledger_store_is_retried.py` already exercises a short lock waited out (0.4 s) and a lock past a lowered bound refused
